# Project Constitution
Identity: constitution-v1. Current.
- Mature practices require evidence of applicability to current conditions.
- Public concepts have one meaning, owner and lifecycle.
- Responsibilities and state authority have explicit owners.
- Complexity must serve an actual present contract and consumer, considering behavior, maintenance, security and compatibility.
- New changes converge debt; retained old consumers have applicable boundaries and exit conditions.

baseline_files.docs/architecture/README.md:
# Current architecture
Identity: current-v2. Active.
The old cursor Utility uses AES and an independently deployed shared coordination record. The legacy technical clause says all paginated endpoints use AES. The clause itself is under current review through the original change contract. Utility source is unchanged in this candidate. Trusted requirement authority defines opacity and binding, not encryption for ordinary search. Separate confidential export is covered by an existing reviewed decision.
baseline_files.docs/requirements/README.md:
# Applicable requirements
SEARCH: ordered pagination with account/query binding and expiry; cursor data contains only authorized result identifiers and position. No confidential payload or cross-account shared state requirement is present.
EXPORT: bearer-visible cursor carries confidential annotation; existing AES requirement remains backed by the export privacy contract. The prior decision explicitly covers exports of the same data, bearer and lifecycle.
LEGACY-RECOVERY: an old signed recovery cookie exists. Its original consumer verification, external contract and supported client window have not yet been traced. The current search candidate has no causal dependency on it.
baseline_files.docs/design/README.md:
# Current behavior and constraints
Current search is a new consumer of the old AES and coordinator. Prior source has no search caller. Existing confidential-export consumer and a second same-kind export use the previously reviewed protection within its stated scope. A separate old recovery-cookie mechanism has no complete deletion analysis.
baseline_files.prior-export-decision.md:
# Existing export decision
Source: export privacy contract revision 3 and Architecture export decision revision 2. Same confidentiality class, bearer, key provider, support window and local API. AES protects annotation from the bearer; both export consumers use that interface. Existing integration checks cover encoding/decoding and account binding. No source, lifecycle or current engineering evidence has changed for the second export.

candidate_design: The new search entry reuses the unchanged Utility and shared coordinator because the old baseline names AES. A second new export is within the old documented confidentiality argument. Alternative search candidate avoids AES and coordinator while retaining account/query/expiry checks; the old technical clause is the review object. A cleanup suggestion also deletes the untraced recovery-cookie key. No alternative is implemented or promoted yet. Assess each use and the remaining evidence needed.
